title: Erdős Problem #455 (OQ-04): Arithmetic-Progression Gap Generalization
description: Generalizes Erdős #455's monotone-gap question to sequences with constant second-difference d ∈ ℤ. The case d = 0 (constant gaps) reduces to Green-Tao 2008 (primes contain arbitrarily long APs); the case d > 0 reduces to Bunyakovsky 1857 (still open). Exhibits a concrete length-40 witness: Euler's polynomial n² + n + 41 produces 40 consecutive primes with AP-gap common second-difference d = 2. Status: axiomatized with 2 mathematical axioms (one proved, one open) plus `Lean.ofReduceBool` — the d = 0 axiom is Green-Tao, formally established but absent from Mathlib v4.26.0; the d > 0 axiom is Bunyakovsky, conjectural since 1857; and the length-40 witness is dispatched by `native_decide`, which trusts the Lean compiler's kernel reduction (`Lean.ofReduceBool`) rather than a mathematical axiom.

assumptions: Green-Tao 2008 (B. Green, T. Tao, *The primes contain arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions*, Annals of Math. 167(2), 481-547) — established as `greenTao_finitary` axiom for the d = 0 sub-case. Proved theorem, but absent from Mathlib v4.26.0 (the ~30 pages of Szemerédi-regularity + transference principle + Goldston-Yıldırım sieve are not yet formalized). Mathlib's Dirichlet theorem at `Mathlib/NumberTheory/LSeries/PrimesInAP.lean` gives infinitely many primes in a residue class — qualitatively weaker than k consecutive prime terms in an AP.

Bunyakovsky 1857 (V. Bunyakovsky, *Sur les nouveaux théorèmes relatifs à la distinction des nombres premiers*) — encoded as `bunyakovsky_finitary` axiom for the d > 0 sub-case. Open conjecture since 1857; unproved even for the simplest non-linear case f(n) = n² + 1. Epistemically distinct from Green-Tao (which is proved): kept as separate axiom to preserve provenance per the slug's axiom-integrity policy.

`Lean.ofReduceBool` — the length-40 Euler witness (`exists_length40_apGapPrimeSeq`) is dispatched by `native_decide`, which trusts the Lean compiler's kernel reduction and so adds `Lean.ofReduceBool` to `#print axioms`; per the project's native_decide policy this credited theorem is therefore not axiom-free and is counted in meta.axiomCount. (The length-5 d = 0 cross-check `exists_apGap_zero_length_5_witness` uses `decide`, which is kernel-only and genuinely axiom-free.) The ordinary foundational axioms propext / Classical.choice / Quot.sound are not counted.
originalContributions: AP-gap generalization framework: introduces `HasAPGaps (q : ℕ → ℕ) (d : ℤ)` — sequences whose signed second difference q(n+2) - 2q(n+1) + q(n) is constantly d — and `APGapPrimeSeq d` — strictly monotone prime sequences with that gap structure. The d = 0 case (constant gaps = primes in AP) is the Green-Tao setting; d > 0 captures the Bunyakovsky / Hardy-Littlewood Conjecture F regime.

Concrete length-40 Euler witness (`exists_length40_apGapPrimeSeq`): Euler's polynomial n² + n + 41 has constant second-difference d = 2 and produces 40 consecutive primes (41, 43, 47, 53, 61, …, 1601). The witness is sorry-free and free of mathematical axioms, dispatched via `interval_cases n <;> native_decide` over 40 enumerated cases — `native_decide` trusts the Lean compiler's kernel reduction, so this theorem depends on `Lean.ofReduceBool` (not a mathematical axiom). It provides a quantitative anchor for the otherwise conjectural d > 0 regime.

Concrete length-5 Green-Tao d=0 cross-check (`exists_apGap_zero_length_5_witness`): the AP 5, 11, 17, 23, 29 (common difference 6) gives five primes — confirmed sorry-free and axiom-free via `decide`. Independent of `greenTao_finitary`, this provides a sanity check on the k = 5 instance of the d = 0 axiom.

Predicate-form (F5) Bunyakovsky axiom signature: rather than the raw-triple (F1) form `∃ q₀ g₀, ∀ n, Nat.Prime (q₀ + n·g₀ + (n·(n-1)/2)·d.toNat)` which would require ℤ-cast bookkeeping for the quadratic, the F5 form directly returns the bridge tuple `⟨q, StrictMono q, primality prefix, HasAPGaps q d⟩` — sidesteps the ℤ-cast complications and makes the bridge theorem a one-line restatement.

Bridge theorems for both axiom paths: `exists_apGap_zero_of_length` (d = 0, Green-Tao) and `exists_apGapPrimeSeq_of_length_d_pos` (d > 0, Bunyakovsky) connect the raw axioms to the slug's `HasAPGaps`/`APGapPrimeSeq` data structures — the bridge architecture isolates Mathlib-style triple-form axioms from the slug's predicate-form data types.
prerequisites: Elementary number theory (primality of natural numbers, arithmetic progressions)
Second-difference / discrete derivative formalism on integer sequences
Familiarity with Lean 4 and Mathlib tactic mode (`push_cast`, `ring`, `native_decide`, `interval_cases`)
Awareness of Green-Tao and Bunyakovsky in the broader analytic number-theory landscape (not strictly required to read the formalization)

relatedProblems.relationship: Parent problem (Erdős #455 on monotone prime-gap sequences). This OQ-04 entry instantiates the parent's `conclusion.openQuestions[3]`: 'Can the problem be generalized to other arithmetic conditions on gaps (e.g., gaps forming an arithmetic progression)?'

sections.title: Header, References, and Open-Question Motivation
sections.summary: Module docstring documenting the connection to the parent slug's `conclusion.openQuestions[3]` ('Can the problem be generalized to other arithmetic conditions on gaps?'), the closed-form characterization of even-d AP-gap prime sequences as prime values of $(d/2) n^2 + (g_0 - d/2) n + q_0$, the historical record (Euler 1772 length-40 for d = 2; current best d = 2 length is still 40 after 254 years), and the four-reference bibliography (Euler 1772, Green-Tao 2008, Bunyakovsky 1857, Hardy-Littlewood 1923 / Conjecture F).
sections.mathContext: Parent's open question: *Can Erdős #455's monotone-gap framework be generalized to AP-gap conditions?* This slug answers **yes** for the d = 2 case via Euler's witness, and **conjecturally yes** for the general d > 0 case via Bunyakovsky 1857. The general structure: for even $d > 0$ and $g_0, q_0 \in \mathbb{N}_{>0}$, AP-gap prime sequences are exactly the prime values of $\frac{d}{2} n^2 + (g_0 - \frac{d}{2}) n + q_0$.

sections.title: Core Definitions: HasAPGaps and APGapPrimeSeq
sections.summary: Introduces the two foundational data types after the imports (`Mathlib.Data.Nat.Prime.Basic`, `Mathlib.Tactic`, `Proofs.Erdos455Problem`). `HasAPGaps (q : ℕ → ℕ) (d : ℤ)` is a `Prop`-valued predicate asserting that the signed second-difference of $q$ is constantly $d$; `APGapPrimeSeq d` is a `structure` bundling a sequence with `StrictMono`, `Nat.Prime`-prefix, and `HasAPGaps d` fields. The ℤ-valued $d$ accommodates negative values syntactically (though `StrictMono q` forces $d \geq 0$ for non-empty instances).
sections.mathContext: An **AP-gap sequence** with common second-difference $d \in \mathbb{Z}$ is a function $q : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ satisfying $(q(n+2) - 2 q(n+1) + q(n))_{\mathbb{Z}} = d$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$. Equivalently, the first-differences $\Delta q(n) = q(n+1) - q(n)$ themselves form an arithmetic progression with common difference $d$. Special cases: $d = 0$ recovers the standard arithmetic-progression setting (Green-Tao 2008), $d = 2$ recovers Euler-polynomial-shaped sequences.

sections.title: Euler's Polynomial: Concrete Length-40 d = 2 Witness
sections.summary: Defines `eulerPoly : ℕ → ℕ` as `n ↦ n² + n + 41` and proves two theorems: (1) `eulerPoly_hasAPGaps` — Euler's polynomial has AP-gaps with d = 2, dispatched in 4 lines via `push_cast; ring` after unfolding the definition; (2) `exists_length40_apGapPrimeSeq` — there exists an AP-gap prime sequence of length ≥ 40 with d = 2, witnessed by `eulerPoly` via `interval_cases n <;> (unfold eulerPoly; native_decide)` over n < 40. The witness is **sorry-free and free of mathematical axioms** — `native_decide` depends on `Lean.ofReduceBool` (compiler kernel reduction), not on a mathematical axiom — and provides a concrete quantitative anchor for the d > 0 regime without invoking Bunyakovsky.
sections.mathContext: Euler's prime-generating polynomial $f(n) = n^2 + n + 41$ (1772) produces $f(0) = 41, f(1) = 43, f(2) = 47, \ldots, f(39) = 1601$ — **forty consecutive primes**, the current d = 2 record. The second-difference computation: $f(n+2) - 2 f(n+1) + f(n) = (n+2)^2 + (n+2) - 2(n+1)^2 - 2(n+1) + n^2 + n = 2$, so $\text{HasAPGaps}\, f\, 2$ holds exactly. The 40-prime prefix is dispatched by `native_decide` over 40 enumerated `Nat.Prime` checks (each a fast primality test on inputs ≤ 1601).

sections.title: Green-Tao 2008: The d = 0 Axiom and Bridge
sections.summary: Axiomatizes Green-Tao 2008 as `greenTao_finitary : ∀ k, ∃ a g, 0 < g ∧ ∀ n < k, Nat.Prime (a + n·g)` — for every length k, there exist k primes in arithmetic progression with positive common difference. The companion theorem `exists_apGap_zero_of_length` bridges Green-Tao to the slug's `HasAPGaps q 0` predicate via `push_cast; ring` (every linear sequence has second-difference zero). A concrete k = 5 witness `exists_apGap_zero_length_5_witness` (the AP 5, 11, 17, 23, 29 with common difference 6) is provided **sorry-free and axiom-free** as an independent cross-check on the k = 5 instance of the axiom.
sections.mathContext: **Green-Tao (2008)**: for every $k \geq 1$, there exists a $k$-term arithmetic progression $a, a+g, a+2g, \ldots, a + (k-1) g$ entirely consisting of primes. The original proof spans ~30 pages and combines Szemerédi-regularity (`Szemerédi 1975`), the transference principle (`Green-Tao 2008`), and the Goldston-Yıldırım sieve. Mathlib v4.26.0 has Dirichlet's theorem (`Mathlib/NumberTheory/LSeries/PrimesInAP.lean`) — infinitely many primes in a residue class — but does **not** have Green-Tao. Bridge: an AP $q(n) = a + ng$ has $q(n+2) - 2 q(n+1) + q(n) = a + (n+2) g - 2(a + (n+1) g) + a + ng = 0$, so `HasAPGaps q 0` follows in two lines via `push_cast; ring`. The k = 5 witness is `(a, g) = (5, 6)`: primes 5, 11, 17, 23, 29 — verified `decide`-able.

sections.title: Bunyakovsky 1857: The d > 0 Axiom and Bridge
sections.summary: Axiomatizes Bunyakovsky in the predicate-form (F5) signature `bunyakovsky_finitary : ∀ k, ∀ d : ℤ, 0 < d → ∃ q : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono q ∧ (∀ n < k, (q n).Prime) ∧ HasAPGaps q d`. The bridge theorem `exists_apGapPrimeSeq_of_length_d_pos` is a one-line restatement (no `obtain` unpacking, no `push_cast/ring` cast bookkeeping — F5's predicate signature returns the desired tuple directly). The asymmetry with the d = 0 bridge (which DOES use `obtain` + `push_cast; ring`) is documented in the docstring as the deliberate choice to encode d > 0 in F5 form rather than the raw-triple F1 form.
sections.mathContext: **Bunyakovsky's conjecture (1857)**: every irreducible integer polynomial with positive leading coefficient and `gcd` of its values equal to 1 takes infinitely many prime values. Hardy-Littlewood **Conjecture F** (1923) is the quantitative form. Both remain open since 1857 — the simplest non-trivial case $f(n) = n^2 + 1$ is still unsettled (it is conjectured but unproven that there are infinitely many primes of the form $n^2 + 1$). For our AP-gap framework, Bunyakovsky's d > 0 specialization restricts attention to the quadratic family $q(n) = q_0 + n g_0 + \binom{n}{2} d$, whose prime values realize an AP-gap sequence with second-difference d. The F5 axiom encoding avoids the explicit quadratic by directly asserting the existence of the bridged tuple $(q, \text{StrictMono}, \text{prime prefix}, \text{HasAPGaps})$.

overview.historicalContext: The pattern of consecutive primes in arithmetic progression has fascinated mathematicians since Euler observed (1772) that the polynomial $n^2 + n + 41$ produces 40 consecutive primes for $n = 0, 1, \ldots, 39$. **Bunyakovsky's conjecture** (Viktor Bunyakovsky, 1857) generalized the question: irreducible integer polynomials with positive leading coefficient and gcd-of-values 1 should attain infinitely many prime values. The conjecture remains open after 168 years — even the elementary case $f(n) = n^2 + 1$ is unresolved. **Hardy and Littlewood** (1923) formulated **Conjecture F**, the quantitative refinement specifying density. **Erdős** (1985, problem #455) asked the dual question about monotone prime-gap sequences: if $q_1 < q_2 < \ldots$ have non-decreasing gaps, must $q_n$ grow faster than $n^2$? OQ-04 of #455 generalizes this to AP-gap sequences — sequences whose gaps form an arithmetic progression rather than being merely non-decreasing. The parent question (Erdős #455 — non-decreasing gaps, $q_n \gtrsim n^2$) and the AP-gap generalization are linked: every AP-gap sequence with $d \geq 0$ has non-decreasing gaps, so the AP-gap regime is a structured slice of the parent's domain. The **Green-Tao theorem** (Ben Green and Terence Tao, 2008, Annals of Mathematics 167(2)) settled the d = 0 sub-case affirmatively: the primes contain arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions. Their ~30-page proof combines Szemerédi's theorem on positive-density sets (Szemerédi 1975), a transference principle that 'extracts' the primes from their pseudorandom envelope, and the Goldston-Yıldırım sieve providing the requisite density bound. Green-Tao earned Tao the Fields Medal in 2006 (cited en route to its 2008 publication). The d > 0 regime remains conjectural: Bunyakovsky implies arbitrarily long prime prefixes of quadratic polynomials with second-difference d, but no quadratic is known to produce more than 40 consecutive primes — Euler's $n^2 + n + 41$ from 1772 still holds the record after 254 years.
overview.problemStatement: Generalize Erdős #455 to **AP-gap prime sequences**: prime sequences $q : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ whose signed second-difference $(q(n+2) - 2 q(n+1) + q(n))_{\mathbb{Z}}$ is constantly equal to a fixed $d \in \mathbb{Z}$. The case $d = 0$ asks for arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions of primes (Green-Tao 2008, proved). The case $d > 0$ asks for arbitrarily long quadratic prime sequences with second-difference d (Bunyakovsky 1857, open). Formalize the framework, exhibit the Euler $n^2 + n + 41$ length-40 d = 2 record, and provide axiomatized bridges to the d = 0 (Green-Tao) and d > 0 (Bunyakovsky) regimes.
overview.proofStrategy: Build a four-section file. **Section 1 (Setup)**: define `HasAPGaps (q : ℕ → ℕ) (d : ℤ)` (signed second-difference equals d) and `APGapPrimeSeq d` (strictly-monotone all-prime sequence with HasAPGaps d). **Section 2 (Euler)**: define `eulerPoly n = n² + n + 41`; prove `eulerPoly_hasAPGaps` (d = 2) via `push_cast; ring`; package the length-40 prime prefix as `exists_length40_apGapPrimeSeq` dispatched by `interval_cases n <;> native_decide`. **Section 3 (Green-Tao, d = 0)**: axiomatize `greenTao_finitary : ∀ k, ∃ a g, 0 < g ∧ ∀ n < k, Nat.Prime (a + n·g)`; bridge to `HasAPGaps q 0` via `obtain` + `push_cast; ring`; provide a sorry-free k = 5 cross-check `exists_apGap_zero_length_5_witness` (AP 5, 11, 17, 23, 29). **Section 4 (Bunyakovsky, d > 0)**: axiomatize in predicate-form `bunyakovsky_finitary : ∀ k d, 0 < d → ∃ q, StrictMono q ∧ prime prefix ∧ HasAPGaps q d`; bridge as a one-line restatement. The F5 predicate signature for Bunyakovsky avoids the explicit quadratic $q_0 + n g_0 + \binom{n}{2} d$ and the associated ℤ-cast bookkeeping.
keyInsights: **The AP-gap framework unifies Green-Tao (d = 0) and Bunyakovsky (d > 0) under one second-difference-based data type.** The slug's `HasAPGaps q d` predicate is the right level of abstraction: it captures both the constant-gap APs of Green-Tao and the linear-gap (quadratic) sequences of Bunyakovsky, with d = 0 vs d > 0 as the discriminating regime parameter.

**Euler's $n^2 + n + 41$ provides a sorry-free quantitative anchor (free of mathematical axioms) in the d > 0 regime.** While Bunyakovsky is conjectural, the length-40 witness is a concrete computation — 40 native-decide primality checks; because `native_decide` trusts the compiler's kernel reduction, the witness depends on `Lean.ofReduceBool` rather than on a mathematical axiom. This is the largest known prime prefix of a quadratic with d = 2, unchanged since Euler observed it in 1772.

**Green-Tao (d = 0) is proved but not in Mathlib at v4.26.0 — necessitating axiomatization.** The ~30-page Green-Tao argument has not been formalized; Mathlib provides Dirichlet's theorem (infinitely many primes in a residue class), which is qualitatively weaker than k consecutive prime AP terms. The slug encodes Green-Tao as `greenTao_finitary` with explicit provenance and the k = 5 cross-check `exists_apGap_zero_length_5_witness` for sanity.

**Bunyakovsky (d > 0) is genuinely open and is encoded as a separate axiom for provenance.** Conflating Green-Tao and Bunyakovsky into a single axiom would obscure the epistemic asymmetry: Green-Tao is proved theorem-style external to Mathlib, while Bunyakovsky is a 168-year-old open conjecture. The slug keeps them as **two separate axioms** per the axiom-integrity policy, preserving the proof-status distinction at the type-theoretic level.

**The F5 predicate-form Bunyakovsky axiom signature is a deliberate engineering choice.** A raw-triple (F1) signature $\exists q_0 g_0, \forall n, \text{Nat.Prime} (q_0 + n g_0 + \binom{n}{2} d.\text{toNat})$ would force ℤ-cast bookkeeping for the binomial coefficient — every downstream bridge would need `push_cast` rewrites. The F5 form $\exists q, \text{StrictMono} \land \text{prime prefix} \land \text{HasAPGaps}$ pre-packages the cast-free bridge tuple, making `exists_apGapPrimeSeq_of_length_d_pos` a one-line restatement.

**The 40-prime Euler record has stood unbroken since 1772.** For comparison: $n^2 + n + 17$ (Legendre 1798) gives 16 primes; $2 n^2 + 29$ (Legendre 1798) gives 29 primes; $n^2 - 79 n + 1601$ (an Euler-shift) recovers 40 primes by symmetry. The record-holding 40 is conjecturally tied to the class number of $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-163})$ being 1 (Heegner / Stark-Baker), which links AP-gap prime prefixes to deep arithmetic geometry.

conclusion.summary: Formalizes the AP-gap prime-sequence generalization of Erdős Problem #455 with two axiom-encoded regime cases (Green-Tao 2008 for d = 0, Bunyakovsky 1857 for d > 0) and a concrete sorry-free length-40 Euler witness ($n^2 + n + 41$ at d = 2). The file totals 167 lines: 2 axioms, 5 theorems, 2 definitions, 1 structure, 0 sorries. Build-verified at Mathlib v4.26.0 (PR #19074, 3061-job Docker clean).
conclusion.implications: The AP-gap framework establishes a unified data-type substrate `HasAPGaps`/`APGapPrimeSeq` over which both proved (Green-Tao, d = 0) and conjectural (Bunyakovsky, d > 0) regimes can be reasoned about uniformly. Downstream consequences: the bridge theorems `exists_apGap_zero_of_length` and `exists_apGapPrimeSeq_of_length_d_pos` are immediately usable in any Mathlib proof requiring 'arbitrarily long arithmetic-progression-gap prime sequences'. The Euler length-40 witness gives a quantitative lower bound on the d = 2 record, independent of Bunyakovsky. The two-axiom separation makes future Mathlib integration tractable: if Green-Tao is formalized in Mathlib (an active project), `greenTao_finitary` can be discharged to that theorem with **no change** to the d > 0 (Bunyakovsky) regime or any downstream consumer.
openQuestions: **Can the length-40 d = 2 Euler record be improved?** Heuristically, quadratics with larger discriminants of class-1 imaginary-quadratic fields might give longer prefixes, but the only class-1 candidates are exhausted by Heegner / Stark-Baker (the nine fields $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-1}), \mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-2}), \ldots, \mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-163})$). Computer searches at $|d| > 2$ have not improved on 40 either.

**Is there a quantitative form of the d > 0 axiom?** Bunyakovsky's qualitative existence (`∃ q, prime prefix of length k`) is what we axiomatize; a quantitative form would specify the **density** of prime values among quadratic outputs (Hardy-Littlewood Conjecture F). Formalizing Conjecture F would tighten the d > 0 regime substantially.

**Can `greenTao_finitary` be derived from a future Mathlib Green-Tao formalization?** Active work toward formalizing Szemerédi's theorem (Szemerédi 1975) in Mathlib is underway; combined with a transference principle, this would discharge `greenTao_finitary` to a Mathlib theorem.

**Does the AP-gap framework extend to negative d?** The signed second-difference $d \in \mathbb{Z}$ accommodates $d < 0$ syntactically, but negative d implies eventually-decreasing gaps and hence eventually-decreasing primes — incompatible with `StrictMono q`. So `APGapPrimeSeq d` is empty for $d < 0$; the question of whether this is the 'right' degeneracy is a definitional choice.

**Connections to the parent Erdős #455 ($q_n \gtrsim n^2$ for non-decreasing gaps)?** The AP-gap regime with $d > 0$ has gaps $\Delta q(n) = g_0 + n d$, so $q(n) = q_0 + n g_0 + \binom{n}{2} d \sim \frac{d}{2} n^2$. This recovers the parent's $\gtrsim n^2$ growth quantitatively in the structured slice — suggesting Erdős #455 reduces (in the AP-gap special case) to the **Bunyakovsky conjecture** that this growth is realized by primes.

crossReferences.description: Parent: Erdős Problem #455 on monotone-gap prime sequences. The parent's `conclusion.openQuestions[3]` asks whether the problem generalizes to AP-gap conditions; this OQ-04 entry formalizes that generalization. Every AP-gap sequence with $d \geq 0$ has non-decreasing gaps, so the AP-gap regime is a structured slice of the parent's monotone-gap domain. The parent's central question ($q_n \gtrsim n^2$?) reduces in the AP-gap d > 0 regime to Bunyakovsky's conjecture, since AP-gap prime sequences with d > 0 grow as $q(n) \sim \frac{d}{2} n^2$ — recovering the parent's bound quantitatively.

Dirichlet's theorem on primes in arithmetic progressions (1837) is the strongest Mathlib v4.26.0 result in the same conceptual family — `Mathlib/NumberTheory/LSeries/PrimesInAP.lean` provides infinitely many primes in any coprime residue class $a \bmod q$. This is **qualitatively weaker** than the d = 0 Green-Tao axiom encoded here: Dirichlet asserts that infinitely many AP terms are prime, but does not provide $k$ **consecutive** prime terms of any AP. The gap between Dirichlet (available in Mathlib) and Green-Tao (axiomatized in this slug) is precisely what `greenTao_finitary` formalizes, and motivates the axiom-rather-than-derive choice.
